summary: @ornikar/intl-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated sibling payload
details: Package advertised as an i18n/formatjs configuration helper declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs (itself obfuscated with _0xXXXX identifiers) probes the host platform, downloads a pinned Bun runtime archive (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the bun binary to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB Bun-compiled CJS bundle beginning with '// @bun @bun-cjs', packed with a rotated ~2000-entry string array and a character-decoder function (obfuscator.io-style string-array packing) — no readable API surface. The filename does not correspond to any i18n functionality, and the payload's behavior cannot be audited without execution. The alternate-runtime path (Bun) also bypasses Node-only supply-chain scanners on installer machines. Installing this version runs opaque attacker-shipped code on the host at npm install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
